title: Foreign Domestic Workers Borrowing from Licensed Moneylenders
what_it_is: Foreign Domestic Workers Borrowing from Licensed Moneylenders

sections.label: FDW moneylender borrowing study
sections.summary: MOM and MinLaw studied reasons for the surge in FDWs borrowing from licensed moneylenders, with first-loan gaps of seven and six years for 2017 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) for each year in the past five years, among foreign domestic workers (FDWs) found to have borrowed money from licensed moneylenders, what is the median number of months between their first arrival in Singapore and the first loan they take; and (b) whether the Ministry can provide an update on whether a study has been conducted on this issue and, if so, what are the top three reasons for the sharp rise in the number of FDWs borrowing from licensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: And for those who took up their first loan in 2017 and 2018, it is seven years and six years respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) have studied the reasons for the surge in FDWs' borrowing in recent years.

sections.label: Measures curbing Work Pass borrowing
sections.summary: MOM and MinLaw announced aggregate loan caps, a self-exclusion framework and penalties in October 2018, and further measures in July.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To curb the rise in borrowing by Work Pass holders, MOM and MinLaw had announced in October 2018 the introduction of aggregate loan caps, the self-exclusion framework and administrative penalties on Work Pass holders who borrow from unlicensed moneylenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In July this year, just about two months ago, MinLaw announced further measures to stem the increase in moneylending activities targeting foreigners earning less than $10,000 per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The aggregate loan caps for foreigners earning less than $10,000 per annum were reduced and limits were placed on the supply of loans to foreigners.

sections.label: FDW loan numbers 2016 to 2019
sections.summary: Moneylenders Credit Bureau data show 1,500 FDWs took licensed moneylender loans in 2016 and 39,000 in the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Based on the data from the Moneylenders Credit Bureau, from March 2016 to June 2019, the number of FDWs who took loans from LMLs in 2016 was 1,500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And just in the first half of this year, it is 39,000.

sections.label: Reduced aggregate loan cap
sections.summary: The aggregate loan cap was reduced from $1,500 to $500 and limits were placed on the number of foreigners licensed moneylenders can lend to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In terms of the measures we highlighted in July, we have reduced the aggregate loan cap from $1,500 to $500 and we have also limited the number of foreigners that the LMLs can lend to in their loan book and so on.
